bib.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation", Philippe Laban, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yingbo Zhou, Jennifer Neville (Microsoft Research, Salesforce Research). Preprint, arXiv:2505.06120v1, 9 May 2025. The PDF names no conference or journal.

COVERAGE: 155,603 of 155,603 chars, 36 of 36 pages, read in sequence, including the appendices and prompts. References were skimmed for origins. Figures and tables were read only as extracted text, and no images were viewed.

CLAIMS
Shared setup for the main experiment (claims 1-5), p7-8:
- 600 sharded instructions across 6 tasks: Code, Database, Actions, Math, Data-to-text, Summary.
- 15 LLMs, 3 simulation types (FULL, CONCAT, SHARDED), N=10 per model and type, T=1.
- The user simulator, strategy classifier and answer extractor are all prompt-based GPT-4o-mini (p4-5).
- The assistant gets a minimal system instruction and is not told the conversation is multi-turn or underspecified (p5).
- Max response is 1,000 tokens, or 10,000 for o3 and R1 (p25).

1. - claim: Every tested model does worse when the same task is revealed over several turns than when given in one turn.
   number: -39% average (FULL to SHARDED)
   setup: Main experiment. This is the mean of per-task percentage drops. See PROBLEMS for the -35% and 25-point variants.
   quote: "every model sees its performance degrade on every task when comparing FULL and SHARDED performance, with an average degradation of -39%."
   where: p8

2. - claim: The loss is mostly unreliability, not lost best-case ability.
   number: aptitude -16%; unreliability +112%
   setup: Main experiment. Aptitude is the per-instruction 90th-percentile score. Unreliability is the 90th minus 10th percentile, averaged over the corpus.
   quote: "Model aptitude degrades in a non-significant way between the full and sharded settings, with an average drop of 16%. On the other hand, unreliability skyrockets with an average increase of 112% (more than doubling)."
   where: p10

3. - claim: All models are about equally unreliable in multi-turn, regardless of single-turn strength.
   number: about 50 points, best to worst run
   setup: Main experiment, fixed instruction.
   quote: "all models we test exhibit very high unreliability, with performance degrading 50 percent points on average between the best and worst simulated run for a fixed instruction."
   where: p10

4. - claim: The drop comes from underspecification across turns, not from information lost in sharding.
   number: CONCAT = 95.1% of FULL
   setup: Same shards joined as a single-turn bullet list. Instructions were pre-filtered to keep only those with P_CONCAT >= 0.8 P_FULL (p20), so this control is partly selected for.
   quote: "CONCAT performance averaging 95.1% of the FULL counterpart."
   where: p8

5. - claim: Reasoning models get lost like the others, and write longer responses.
   number: 33% longer
   setup: o3 and Deepseek-R1 against the non-reasoning LLMs. The authors call length a "potential root cause".
   quote: "reasoning models tend to generate lengthier responses (on avg. 33% longer than non-reasoning LLMs)."
   where: p9

6. - claim: Two turns are enough to trigger the effect, and only giving everything at once helps.
   number: two-shard threshold. Figure 6c, GPT-4o unreliability: 19% at 1 shard, 49% at 2, 71% at 8. GPT-4o-mini: 32% at 1, 45% at 2, 56% at 8.
   setup: 31 instructions expanded to 248 (1-8 shards each), N=10, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini only (p10, p29).
   quote: "any conversation that involves underspecification and occurs in two or more turns leads to models getting lost in conversation."
   where: p10; Figure 6c p9

7. - claim: Repeating earlier user turns helps partly, and does not reach single-turn performance.
   number: "15-20%". Table 2, GPT-4o-mini: 86.8 / 84.4 / 50.4 / 66.5 / 61.8. GPT-4o: 93.0 / 90.9 / 59.1 / 76.6 / 65.3.
   setup: Code, Database, Math, Actions; N=10; 2 models. Column order is read as FULL, CONCAT, SHARDED, RECAP, SNOWBALL because the headers were lost. RECAP is called unrealistic, since it needs to know which turn is last.
   quote: "SNOWBALL gives a sense of realistic performance gains achievable through user-turn repetition: it can mitigate the FULL-to-SHARDED performance deterioration by 15-20%."
   where: p11. See PROBLEMS: the table does not obviously give this figure.

8. - claim: Lowering temperature fixes single-turn reliability but not multi-turn reliability.
   number: 50-80% drop single-turn; about 15-20% or none in SHARDED; about 30 unreliability left at T=0 for both user and assistant (Table 3: 30.5 for GPT-4o-mini, 29.7 for GPT-4o)
   setup: 40 instructions (10 each from Code, Database, Actions, Math), GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, 20 runs per condition, assistant and user temperature in {0, 0.5, 1} (p30).
   quote: "Even when both the user and assistant temperatures are set to 0.0, there remains a large unreliability of around 30%."
   where: p11

9. - claim: Answering early goes with worse results.
   number: 30.9 (first attempt in first 20% of turns) vs 64.4 (last 20%)
   setup: Code and Math only, across all models; the other four tasks attempt an answer from turn 1 in most cases. Observational binning, not an intervention. The causal mechanism is stated as a hypothesis.
   quote: "conversations with the first attempt being made in the first 20% of conversations achieve a score of 30.9, less than half of the 64.4 when the LLM waits for the last 20% of the conversation to make an answer attempt."
   where: p22

10. - claim: Answers grow over turns because models build on earlier wrong assumptions instead of discarding them.
    number: final attempts 20-300% longer; correct Code 27% longer (850 vs 668 chars); correct SQL 14% longer (129 vs 113 chars)
    setup: Extracted answers, shown for Code, Database, Data-to-text, Summary (Figure 9). The growth per attempt is reported for three of them. Correct-solution lengths are Code and Database, score 100.0 only.
    quote: "the LLM does not successfully invalidate its prior assumptions and overly relies on its previous attempts."; "tend to be 20-300% longer than the solutions generated in the FULL and CONCAT settings."
    where: p23

11. - claim: Lost-in-the-middle also happens across turns: first- and last-turn documents are cited more than middle-turn ones.
    number: eighth-turn summaries, 20% cite turn 8 vs 8% each for turns 2 and 3; first-turn 13% (Figure 10)
    setup: Summary task, averaged over the LLMs; the paper says 15, though OLMo2 and Phi-4 have no Summary scores in Table 1. Effect size varies by model, and model-level results are not included. Row totals under 100% are hallucinated citations.
    quote: "In eighth-turn summaries, 20% of citations are to documents introduced in turn 8, compared to 8% from turn 2 and 3 (150% difference)."
    where: p23-24

12. - claim: Longer responses go with lower scores on five of six tasks.
    number: 10-50% higher for the shortest quintile
    setup: Quintiles within each (LLM, instruction) pair. Actions is the exception. Correlational; the assumption mechanism is a hypothesis.
    quote: "On five of the six tasks, performance is 10-50% higher in simulated conversations with shortest response length, compared to conversations with longest response length."
    where: p24

13. - claim: Episodic tasks that decompose by turn do not degrade, so the effect needs underspecified, non-decomposable generation.
    number: BLEU within 10%. Table 4: 41.7 / 43.4 / 42.1 for GPT-4o-mini, 35.9 / 38.5 / 40.9 for GPT-4o.
    setup: Translation, 30 German-English documents truncated to 10 sentences, 5 shards of two sentences (p28). The authors note BLEU may miss document-level nuance. The three required task properties are stated as a hypothesis.
    quote: "with BLEU scores being within 10% difference of each other in all settings."
    where: p12

14. - claim: Simulator error is small, and does not explain the drop.
    number: under 5% of conversations had errors; under 2% were disfavoured; about 98% valid
    setup: Manual inspection of Actions, Code, Math, Database only.
    quote: "errors introduced by the user simulator, strategy classifier, or answer extraction occurred in less than 5% of inspected conversations and that these errors disfavored the assistant model in less than 2% of the conversations."
    where: p5; Table 5 p20

15. - claim: The authors advise users to restart, and to consolidate requirements before retrying.
    number: none
    setup: Advice inferred from CONCAT results and a Reddit anecdote about Cursor. No experiment tests a mid-conversation LLM consolidation or a fresh restart. The authors call both "patched solutions".
    quote: "starting a new conversation that repeats the same information might yield significantly better outcomes than continuing an ongoing conversation."
    where: p12

16. - claim: The authors set a target for a reliable LLM.
    number: U < 15 at T=1.0 in multi-turn
    setup: A proposed target, not a measured result.
    quote: "have small unreliability (U 9010 < 15) in multi-turn settings"
    where: p11

LIMITS
Conceded by the authors (p3, p13):
- Simulated conversations are "not representative of natural human-AI conversation": narrow structure, one new shard per turn, intent always in turn 1, and all information available by the end.
- Minimal shards are "unrealistic and potentially adversarial". The authors rely on gradual sharding to answer this, but it covers only two models.
- They argue the result is "most likely an underestimate", which is an argument, not a measurement.
- Only analytical, text-only, English tasks. Creative tasks are untested.

Not shown:
- No human users, no agent loops with tool execution, and no compaction or memory.
- Not a window-occupancy study. Only Summary is described as testing long context. No result is tied to how full the window is, and the effect appears at two turns. For the target note, this is a different mechanism from "occupancy grows; recall degrades", and it does not support the note's ~50% threshold or its claim of monotonic decline with session length.
- The nearest fit in the note's taxonomy is a model's own wrong assumptions persisting, as in poisoning (claim 10; p9 also mentions confusing user requirements with its own earlier turns). The paper does not use that vocabulary.
- Claim 7 is relevant to the note's "repeating the constraint" anti-fix, but it tests repeating user turns over two models, not forceful repetition.
- Default behaviour only. A system prompt encouraging clarification is untested, and the authors say it would likely change behaviour (p5).
- Mechanism claims 9-12 are observational or hypothesised.
- Sub-experiments use only GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, so they do not generalise to 15 models.

Dated: the model set is from May 2025 (GPT-4.1, o3, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 previews, Llama 4 Scout).

BUILDS ON
- Herlihy et al. 2024 [27]: underspecification in logs, response categories.
- Zipf 1949 [91]: principle of least effort.
- Liu et al. 2024 [50], Huang et al. 2023 [29], Laban et al. 2024 [40]: loss in the middle.
- Zheng et al. 2023 [89]: MT-bench, the episodic baseline it contrasts with.
- Liu et al. 2022 [51]: atomic content units.
- Choi et al. 2021 [13]: decontextualization.
- Chang et al. 2025 [7]: users reveal the full instruction "34% of the time".
- Belem et al. 2024 [3]: mini-Haystacks.
- Zhong et al. 2020 [90]: SQL evaluation.
- Papineni et al. 2002 [58]: BLEU.
- Datasets: HumanEval (Chen 2021), LiveCodeBench (Jain 2024), Spider (Yu 2018), BFCL (Yan 2024), GSM8K (Cobbe 2021), ToTTo (Parikh 2020), Summary of a Haystack (Laban 2024), WMT 2019 (Scherrer 2019).

CODE
- Metrics, p7: `A90 = percentile90(S) U 9010 = percentile90(S) − percentile10(S).`
- Snowball prompt, p30: `Just to reiterate:\n - [past utterance 1]\n- [past utterance 2]\n\n Also,\n[current utterance].`
- User simulator persona, p34: `The user is inherently lazy, and answers in short form, providing only minimal information to the system.`
- Sharding acceptance rule, p20: `P CONCAT ≥ 0.8 P FULL` and `P SHUFFLE -CONCAT ≥ 0.8 P FULL`

FIGURES (captions shortened; contents judged from extracted text only)
- Figure 1, p1: "we simulate single- and multi-turn conversations for six generation tasks." Shows the premature attempt, wrong assumption and bloat story alongside the aptitude and unreliability shift, all on one panel.
- Figure 6, p9: Aptitude and Unreliability box plots, 15-model results, gradual sharding. Best single evidence figure; shows the gap widening for all models and at two shards.
- Figure 10, p24: citation heatmap by turn. Shows loss-in-middle-turns at a glance.
- Figure 4, p5: the five simulation types. Explains FULL, CONCAT, SHARDED, RECAP and SNOWBALL faster than prose.
- Figure 9, p23: answer length by attempt number. Shows answer bloat directly.
- Figure 11, p29: worked Math conversation with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, showing invented pastries derailing the result (correct answer 85,000; extracted 45,000).
- Figure 2, p4: paired full and sharded instruction. Defines sharding by example.

PROBLEMS
Inconsistencies within the paper. Cite the specific number and setup:
- Headline drop: -39% (abstract, p8), -35% (Figure 1, p1), and "average performance of 65%–a 25-point drop from single-turn performances of 90%" (p2). The paper does not reconcile them. My own average of Table 1's last column is about 61, which matches -39%.
- Aptitude: -16% in the text (p10), -15% in Figure 1. It is also called "non-significant" with no test reported.
- Inspection size: "several hundred" (p5), "200" (p20), and "100" in the Table 5 caption (p20).
- Gradual sharding: Appendix K says "a total of eight instructions across three tasks", then "the 31 instructions" and 248 total. 31 x 8 = 248, and p10 also says 31, so "eight" looks like an error.
- Section 6.3 calls maximality "property P3", but Appendix B lists it as P4.
- Table 1's caption says the last two columns average "performance drops", but the values (for example 62.5) read as percent of FULL retained.
- "15-20%" (claim 7) is not obviously derivable from Table 2. My own calculation gives Snowball recovering about 31% of the FULL-SHARDED gap for GPT-4o-mini and about 18% for GPT-4o, or 11.4 and 6.2 points. Check before restating it.
- The conclusion calls agent-like concatenation "ineffective" (p13), while p11 reports partial improvement.
- "for every single model, conversations with a later first answer attempt lead to higher averaged performance" (p22) is not strictly monotonic in Table 6: OLMo2 drops 47.3 to 26.4 and R1 drops 66.4 to 50.2 in the last bin; Llama 4 Scout drops 39.8 to 36.8 early.
- Figure 6c (claim 6): GPT-4o unreliability rises from 49% to 71% between 2 and 8 shards, which sits uneasily with "granularity...does not majorly impact reliability" (p10).
- Summary size: "around twenty documents" and 10 shards in the text (p7, p28), against a 12-document example in Figure 5 and 8 turns in Figure 10.

Extraction faults:
- Icon column headers in Tables 1, 2 and 4 were lost; I inferred order from captions and the surrounding text.
- Figure 6 numbers come as loose text, and I read each triple as unreliability, aptitude, floor. Check these against the image before quoting.
- Stray citation key in the text at p5: "simulatesouthworth2023developingd".
- Line wraps in quotes are collapsed to spaces.

Embedded instructions: none aimed at a reader. The prompts in Appendix O are the paper's own experimental materials, and I treated them as data.
